# Ontology Modelling: TBox and ABox

An RDF knowledge base splits into two halves that live in the same triple store but answer different
questions:

- **TBox** (terminology) — the schema. What classes exist, how they specialise each other, what
  properties connect them, what their domains and ranges are. *"A Builder is a User is a Person is
  an Agent."*
- **ABox** (assertions) — the instances. *"`mc:alice` is a `mc:Builder`."*

The split is what makes a **reasoner** useful. Load both, and the store can derive facts nobody
wrote: assert `mc:alice a mc:Builder`, and RDFS inference over `rdfs:subClassOf` answers "list all
Agents" with Alice in it. In a relational schema the same question needs a join the modeller
anticipated; here it needs no query change at all.

## How lab 5 realises it

`Information-Systems-Modelling` lab 5 keeps the halves in separate Turtle files under
`src/main/resources/`, and `App.java` loads them into an in-memory [[rdf4j]] repository wrapped in an
RDFS inferencer:

| File | Role | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| `ontology.ttl` | TBox — the ModellingClub vocabulary | 577 |
| `sample-data.ttl` | ABox — instances | 209 |

The TBox declares a real taxonomy rather than a flat list of types: **24 `rdfs:subClassOf`
statements**, rooted at `mc:Agent` → `mc:Person` / `mc:SystemAccount`, then `mc:User` → `mc:AdminUser`
/ `mc:Builder`, each class carrying an `rdfs:label` and an `rdfs:comment`. Every term is namespaced
under `http://modellingclub.local/ontology#` and the ontology resource itself carries `owl:Ontology`
metadata with a Dublin Core title, description and creator.

Eight SPARQL `SELECT` queries run against the loaded store. Two of them exist specifically to prove
the reasoner is doing work rather than the data: `listInferredKnowsLinks` (a symmetric property
returning links nobody asserted in that direction) and `listTransitiveCommunityMembership`. The
others — builds with creators, approved builds by score, drone telemetry, votes per build,
marketplace listings, test-run attendees — are ordinary retrieval.

`SampleDataWriter.addAdditionalUser` also writes triples programmatically before querying, so the
same store is exercised through both a file loader and the RDF4J model API.

## Where the TBox goes next

The identical `ontology.ttl` reappears in `lab6/vocabulary/` and becomes the fallback vocabulary for
[[linked-data-publishing]] — where schema.org has no term, the `mc:` term from this TBox is used
instead. See [[schema-org-first-custom-vocab-fallback]].

The two copies are **byte-identical rather than shared**, which is a small instance of
[[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]] and sits awkwardly beside lab 6's own headline principle
that no fact should be written twice.

## Unused ABoxes left in the tree

`instances.ttl` (557 lines — larger than the ABox actually loaded), `cardinalityTest.owl`,
`convert.py`, `ontology_instances.rdf` and `ontology_instances.jsonld` are all tracked in the same
`resources/` directory and referenced by **no code, README or pom**. `App.java` loads
`ontology.ttl` and `sample-data.ttl` only.
